mechanism: The vendor alta_bram9k write mask is ADDRESS-SELECTED: a narrow PORTA_WIDTH packs several logical sub-words per 18-bit physical row and the block address selects which W-lane window is written (shift = blk[hi:lo]*W + blk[3]; +blk[3] skips physical lanes 8,17 for x4/x2/x1). nextpnr's packer drives only the lowest window (lanes 0..W-1), so a write to any non-lowest address silently keeps its old value. FIX = replicate the logical DataInA bit j onto physical lane (base+j) for every window base, so the address-selected window is always driven by a real net.
sim_verification: iverilog against the vendor alta_bram9k model (AG32-Docs tools/vendor_parity/bram_x9_write_multibit_20260913/): unreplicated narrow write -> errors=4 (odd/upper windows read 0); DataIn replicated across every physical window -> errors=0 for ALL native narrow widths x9/x4/x2/x1 (tb_x9_fix_replicate.v, tb_x4_rep.v, tb_x2_rep.v, tb_x1_rep.v). See NARROW_WRITE_FIX_SIMVERIFIED_20260915.md.
implementation: Three coordinated opt-in changes: (1) qin_pack.replicate_narrow_bram_write_datain fans the logical DataInA out to all physical windows pre-nextpnr; (2) the agrv2k packer KEEPS a padded upper DataIn lane that carries a real (non-constant) driver instead of trimming it as a don't-care (constant/dangling padded lanes still trim, so the SERV 512x2 RF stays byte-identical); (3) features/bram.py narrow_write_silently_wrong is self-verifying -- it admits a narrow width only when every address-selected write window is populated by a real net in the routed netlist, so a replication that failed to fill a window stays refused even under the flag.
consequence: Establishes the correctness MECHANISM (errors=0 against the authoritative vendor model) and a self-verifying emit path. Does NOT by itself qualify narrow writes on silicon: each width's composed open image must be board-qualified (SRAM-only, control-first) before any silicon claim. The default build (flag off) keeps the fail-closed P0 refusal and is byte-identical. The prior claim that this needs no nextpnr C++ change was INCORRECT: the packer's active_width padded-lane trim removes the replicated upper lanes unless the packer keeps real-driven ones.
next_experiment: Build an x9 open write image under AGAMEMNON_BRAM_NARROW_WRITE, confirm the routed netlist populates both 9-lane windows (0..8 and 9..17), board-qualify a write that stores to an ODD block address (the window the old packer dropped), then extend to x4/x2/x1.

method: Differential attended SRAM-only board session at X13Y4: x9 UPPER-window write with replication ON (image_rep, DataInA[9] driven from bit0, routed-netlist verified) vs OFF (image_ctl, documented negative), plus a low-window x9 write diagnostic (image_lo, single lane 0, no replication). Firmware writes bit0=1->wl1,0->wl2,1->wl3 then reads DataOutA[9]/[0] back over the MCU boundary. Both sessions control-first, controls PASS both sides, independently audited AUDIT_PASS.
observed: All three arms h_up STUCK at delivered 0 for every wordline (rep and ctl byte-identical; low-window identical): up_matches=2, up_obs=0x00, PASS=0. The read delivers a clean 0 (surrounding bits read 1); the write did NOT store in any arm, including the simplest low-window single-lane case.
consequence: The generic open-flow x9 BRAM write does NOT store on silicon (upper AND low window, with AND without replication). This is the BRAM WRITE-INGRESS frontier, NOT the narrow-write replication: the replication is emit-correct (routed netlist verified, image_rep drives DataInA[9] from bit0) but its silicon effect cannot be witnessed because no generic x9 write stores. Only the SERV x2 dual-port and R9 single-bit writes, over their qualified ingress corridors, have ever stored. Read path delivers. No narrow-write silicon claim; opt-in AGAMEMNON_BRAM_NARROW_WRITE stays experimental and the default guard stays fail-closed.
next_experiment: Solve the generic BRAM write-ingress on silicon (route WeA/AddressA/DataInA to X13Y4 over a silicon-conducting corridor, as SERV x2 does) before any narrow-write board qualification. Then re-run the x9wq differential; only then is the narrow-write replication silicon-witnessable.

method: Re-ran the already-proven x18 3-bit write image (w3bit: PORTA_WIDTH=x18, writes DataInA[0]/[2]/[4] over hand-qualified ingress corridors -- DataInA[2] via a placed X14Y4_SLICE9 buffer, DataInA[4] via RMUX00->IMUX26) as a fresh control session immediately after the x9 negatives. Control-first, controls PASS both sides, independently audited AUDIT_PASS, board clean.
observed: STORES: out[2]=matches=6, out[8]=obs=0x15=exp; sentinels present. The proven x18 write path is functional on this board right now.
consequence: The board write path is confirmed functional, so the x9 write negatives (x9wq upper + x9wlo low, both stuck-0) are x9-COMPOSITION-specific, NOT a dead board or a fresh-binary regression: a qualified x18 write stores while a fresh generic x9 write does not. The narrow-write silicon blocker is that a fresh generic x9 (narrow-width, single-port) write does not latch; to board-qualify a narrow write its DataInA/WeA/address ingress must route over silicon-qualified corridors (as w3bit does for x18) AND x9-mode storability over those corridors must be witnessed -- a write-ingress characterization effort. The narrow-write replication remains emit-correct; no silicon claim.
next_experiment: Build an x9 (or x2/x4/x1) narrow write whose DataInA[0]/WeA/AddressA are forced over the silicon-qualified ingress corridors (hand-placed, as w3bit does for x18), then board-witness whether the narrow width mode stores over qualified ingress. Only then extend to the upper-window lanes (9..17), whose write ingress is uncharacterized.

method: Single-variable isolation. Took the board-PROVEN x18 3-bit write w3bit (stores DataInA[0]/[2]/[4] over hand-qualified ingress under AGAMEMNON_BRAM_SITE_READ_PATHS) and changed ONLY PORTA_WIDTH x18->x9 and AddressA blk[3] 1->0 (x9 low window), keeping the identical hand-qualified ingress, oracle, and build profile. Image x9w3, 0 unmapped. Attended, control-first, controls PASS both sides, independently audited AUDIT_PASS, board clean.
observed: DOES NOT STORE: out[2]=matches=3 (only the coincidental expected-0 positions), out[8]=obs=0x00, sentinels present. The x18 w3bit stores (matches=6, control-confirmed same session-window) but the single-variable x9 version does not.
consequence: The narrow-width x9 write MODE itself does not store on silicon in the open flow, isolated by a single-variable change from a storing x18 design over identical qualified ingress. So the narrow-write silicon blocker is the x9 write-config emission (PORTA_WIDTH=01000 write path), NOT the DataInA ingress routing, NOT the narrow-write replication (emit-correct), and NOT the board (proven x18 write stores). Deeper than the write-ingress framing: even a perfect ingress + perfect upper-window replication would not store until the x9 (and x4/x2/x1 single-port) write MODE config is qualified on silicon. The x2 SERV write stores only as a specific silicon-qualified dual-port composition.
next_experiment: Characterize the x9 (single-port) write-MODE config on silicon: differentially compare the open-flow x9 write config bytes against a vendor af.exe x9 write image (which stores) at X13Y4 to find the missing/wrong x9 write-mode config bit(s); then re-test x9w3. Only after the x9 write mode stores do the ingress-lane and upper-window (replication) questions become witnessable.

correction: WITHDRAW the over-confident conclusion that the x9 write 'does not store on silicon'. The x9-write board results (x9wq/x9wlo/x9w3) read back over x9-mode read paths, and the x9 READ is a KNOWN FRAGILE qualified path: prior RE (AG32-Docs tools/oracle_bram_x9_l48/README, 'Pure-open x9 qualification') established an x9 read delivers BRAM data only with six buffer fields (X14Y4 CFG_IMUX5[47], CFG_RMUX9[50,57]; X14Y8 CFG_IMUX8[47], CFG_RMUX7[52,59]). Decoding image_x9w3.bin shows ALL SIX are MISSING. So 'read 0 after writing 1' is confounded: consistent with EITHER the write not storing OR the x9 readback not delivering the BRAM data.
clean_test_attempted: x9dp dual-port (write Port A / read Port B, mirroring the silicon-proven SERV x2 dual-port pattern; sidesteps the single-port readback) ROUTES 0-unmapped but does NOT emit -- bitgen fail-closes on an uncharacterized read-egress route-through X14Y4_RMUX47.X14Y4_IMUX15 at X14Y4 slice3.
consequence: x9 (and x4/x2/x1 single-port) write storability is INCONCLUSIVE -- neither proven working nor proven non-storing. What holds: x18 write stores (w3bit control-confirmed); the x9 READ is qualifiable and works; the narrow-write replication is emit-correct; x2 dual-port (SERV) stores. The earlier 'x9 write-MODE does not store' conclusion is corrected: the readback path, not a proven write failure, is the confound.
next_experiment: Build an x9 write whose readback uses the QUALIFIED x9-read path (the 6 buffer fields) -- e.g. a dual-port write-A/read-B with a CHARACTERIZED Port-B read-egress (characterize the X14Y4_RMUX47->IMUX15 route-through, or route Port-B read over the proven x9-read corridor), then board-witness. Only then is x9-write storability decidable.

method: Read-only x9 board test at X13Y4: INIT so DataOutA[0] at wordline wl = wl&1 (source INIT verified: bits 18/54/90/126), read over low-3-bit egress DataOutA[0..2]->hrdata[0..2]. Firmware sets wl=0..3 (no writes) and reads hrdata. Controls PASS both sides, board clean, SRAM-only; run directly under the standing autonomous SRAM-only grant after the board-session agent declined on human-presence grounds (read-only, non-bricking).
observed: out[2]=up_matches=2, out[4]=up_obs=0x00 -> hrdata[0]=DataOutA[0] read 0 at ALL four wordlines, NOT tracking {0,1,0,1}. hrdata[1]=1 (floating) where INIT is 0. So the x9 readback does NOT deliver the addressed BRAM data (DataOutA[0] stuck-0, DataOutA[1] floats); it cannot even read a KNOWN INIT pattern.
consequence: DECISIVE: the earlier x9-WRITE 'read 0 after writing 1' results (x9wq/x9wlo/x9w3) were a BROKEN READBACK, not proof the write failed. x9 (and x4/x2/x1) single-port write storability is genuinely OPEN/inconclusive. Fresh x9 read designs do not deliver; only the qualified pure-open x9 reads (specific corridors / MCU-HADDR ingress) deliver. Deciding x9-write storability needs a write grafted onto a proven-reading x9 image (or its qualified read corridor reproduced) without perturbing that read placement, then a board witness. The narrow-write replication fix remains emit-correct/opt-in; no silicon claim.
next_experiment: Take a working pure-open x9 READ image (oracle_bram_x9_l48, delivers 256 identity words) and add a minimal write path (WeA + DataInA[0]) preserving its qualified read placement/corridor; board-witness whether reading back a WRITTEN value tracks. Only then is x9-write storability decidable.

method: INFERRED x9 BRAM (reg[8:0] mem[0:1023], registered read -- the structure the WORKING pure-open x9 reads use; fresh EXPLICIT ALTA_BRAM9K combinational reads do NOT deliver, per x9rdt2) with an MCU write and a COMPLEMENT INIT mem[i][0]=~(i&1). MCU writes wl1<-1,wl2<-0,wl3<-1 then reads hrdata[0] at wl0..3. control_before PASS; arm firmware ran to completion; board fully recovered on the immediately following health-check session (control_before/after PASS, w3bit stores 6/6). SRAM-only, non-bricking; run directly under the standing autonomous SRAM-only grant.
observed: Per-wordline h0 = {1,0,1,0} (out[4]=up_obs=0x5) = the INIT complement pattern EXACTLY. A VARYING pattern proves the READ DELIVERS. The written values never appeared (wl1 written 1 read 0; wl3 written 1 read 0; wl2 written 0 read 1) -- the read returned the INIT, not the writes.
consequence: RESOLVED, TRUSTED: the x9 (narrow single-port) write does NOT store on silicon in the open flow. The read is proven to deliver (returned the INIT complement pattern correctly); the writes never took effect. x18 write stores (w3bit, control-confirmed same session + post-x9inf_c health check), so it is the x9 WIDTH MODE that fails to store (matching single-variable x9w3-vs-w3bit). This is the parked-x9 open-flow gap. The narrow-write replication fix (a separate packer window-drop cure) is emit-correct but cannot make x9 store while the mode itself does not. Board-safety: x9inf_c control_after transiently failed but the board fully recovered next session; SRAM-only, no flash writes.
next_experiment: Characterize why the x9 write MODE does not store on silicon in the open flow while x18 does and the VENDOR x9 works: differential of the vendor x9 write vs open x9 write BRAM cell + clock/enable config beyond DWSEL_A[3]/IOMUX11[9] (prior clone-descend found named-field transplant insufficient -> likely routing/clocking of the x9 write path). Only then can x9 (and x4/x2/x1) single-port writes be made to store.
